skill.name: performance-analysis
skill.description: Analyze Claude Flow swarm performance, detect bottlenecks, generate reports, and recommend practical optimizations.
skill.summary: Find Claude Flow swarm bottlenecks and turn performance metrics into prioritized improvements.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: All 64 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed examples, documentation links, or context-free pattern matching. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found. One medium supply-chain risk remains because the npx commands do not pin a package version.

remediation.issue: The examples execute an unpinned NPM package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version and use a lockfile or verified package integrity in automated environments.

remediation.issue: The custom integration demonstrates child_process.exec with a command string.
remediation.suggestion: Use execFile with a fixed executable and argument array to prevent command injection if future inputs become dynamic.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned NPM Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: Examples repeatedly run npx claude-flow without a package version. A compromised or unexpectedly changed registry release could execute during analysis.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The quick-start examples directly show unversioned npx execution. This creates a recognized dependency supply-chain risk despite the legitimate package purpose.

content.value_statement: Claude Flow swarms can hide delays across agents, memory, processing, and network operations. This skill identifies bottlenecks and produces prioritized optimization guidance.
actual_capabilities: Detects communication, processing, memory, and network bottlenecks with Claude Flow commands.
Profiles execution time, agent utilization, resource constraints, and operation patterns.
Generates Markdown, HTML, or JSON reports with selected metrics and sections.
Compares current swarm performance with a previous swarm identifier.
Recommends topology, caching, concurrency, priority, and resource adjustments.
Provides CI/CD and Node.js integration examples for recurring analysis.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow commands or MCP tools and accessible swarm metrics.
Does not independently collect telemetry outside the Claude Flow environment.
Estimated improvement percentages are illustrative and require measurement in each environment.
Automatic fixes can change swarm settings and require review before use.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow Swarms
use_cases.description: Find delayed communication, overloaded agents, or inefficient task execution before changing the swarm configuration.

use_cases.title: Track Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare reports after application or workflow changes to identify regressions and validate improvements.

use_cases.title: Enforce Performance Checks
use_cases.description: Generate recurring reports in CI and fail workflows when critical bottlenecks exceed agreed thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Bottleneck Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my current Claude Flow swarm for bottlenecks during the last hour and summarize the three highest-impact issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first review of current swarm performance.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Resource Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Review swarm {swarm_id} for {time_range}, focusing on memory, agent utilization, and task queue delays above {threshold} percent.
prompt_templates.scenario: A targeted investigation with known performance concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative Performance Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current swarm with {baseline_swarm_id} and produce a Markdown report covering regressions, improvements, metrics, and prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Performance Improvement Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {swarm_id}, rank bottlenecks by impact, estimate confidence, propose reversible fixes, and define validation metrics for each change.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced optimization plan with measurable verification.

output_examples.input: Analyze the current swarm for the last hour.
output_examples.output: The report identifies communication delay as the largest bottleneck, followed by memory loading and task queue wait time.

output_examples.input: Compare the current swarm with the previous release.
output: Average task time improved by 12 percent.
Communication latency remains above the target.

output_examples.input: Recommend safe fixes for high cache misses.
output_examples.output: Enable caching in a test environment, measure hit rate and latency, then expand the change only after confirming improvement.

best_practices: Establish a measured baseline before applying any optimization.
Review automatic fixes and test each change in a development environment.
Track the same metrics after every change to confirm impact and detect regressions.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every recommendation at once without isolating its effect.
Do not treat estimated improvement percentages as guaranteed results.
Do not run unpinned packages or automatic fixes in production workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes communication, processing, memory, network, task, and agent performance metrics available through Claude Flow.

faq.question: Does it work without Claude Flow?
faq.answer: No. Its commands, metrics, and examples depend on a configured Claude Flow environment.

faq.question: Can it change my swarm configuration?
faq.answer: Only workflows using the fix option may apply optimizations. Review and test those changes before production use.

faq.question: Which report formats are supported?
faq.answer: The documented command supports Markdown, HTML, and JSON reports with optional metrics and selected sections.

faq.question: Can it compare performance over time?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports time ranges and comparison with a previous swarm identifier when relevant metrics are available.

faq.question: Are the predicted improvements guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Improvement estimates are examples. Validate every recommendation against measured results in your own environment.
